content.text: I've reviewed every payment-adjustment, penalty, and cancellation mechanic in the Agreement and the Statement of Work.

input.quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. IBM's termination of Purchase Orders for its convenience shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum termination charge on IBM, so the preferred position is met. Section 6.1 lets IBM cancel Purchase Orders at any time with no cancellation charge where MSL has defaulted; a convenience cancellation triggers only actual cost reimbursements under the Price section (and, on termination, purchase of Parts/partially completed Product at MSL's cost or a completion-percentage price under Sections 5.2-5.3). Those are reimbursement of demonstrated cost, not a pre-agreed liquidated sum or early-termination fee, so the fallback cap is not engaged. The only stipulated damages mechanics run the other way and benefit us: the delinquent-shipment Profit Rate adjustments (SOW § 7.3 and the delinquency tables), the [*]% responsiveness penalty against MSL, and MSL's obligation to bear Product Recall cost on epidemic failure. Consistent with the playbook, we do not flag amounts payable by Vendor to Customer. No redline proposed.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
